options.D: A disease caused by a nematode

questions.explanation: A fungal plant disease is caused by a fungus or fungus-like organism; examples include rusts, smuts, powdery mildew, downy mildew and many rots.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is bacterial blight?

options.A: A plant disease caused by pathogenic bacteria that can produce water-soaked lesions, blighting or wilting; the exact symptoms depend on crop and pathogen
options.B: A plant disease caused by fungi
options.C: A plant disease caused by viruses
options.D: A plant disease caused by nematodes

questions.explanation: Bacterial blight is caused by pathogenic bacteria that can produce water-soaked lesions, blighting or wilting; the exact symptoms depend on crop and pathogen.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is a viral plant disease?

options.A: A disease caused by a plant virus, often producing mosaic patterns, leaf curling, stunting or yellowing; viruses are commonly transmitted by vectors, seed or planting material
options.B: A disease caused by fungi
options.C: A disease caused by bacteria
options.D: A disease caused by nematodes

questions.explanation: A viral plant disease is caused by a plant virus, often producing mosaic patterns, leaf curling, stunting or yellowing; viruses are commonly transmitted by vectors, seed or planting material.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is rice blast?

options.A: A serious fungal disease of rice caused by Magnaporthe oryzae, producing lesions on leaves and neck or panicle infection
options.B: A bacterial disease of rice caused by Xanthomonas oryzae
options.C: A viral disease of rice
options.D: A nematode disease of rice

questions.explanation: Rice blast is a serious fungal disease of rice caused by Magnaporthe oryzae, producing lesions on leaves and neck or panicle infection.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is bacterial blight of rice?

options.A: A fungal disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae
options.B: A bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae, often causing leaf blighting and drying
options.C: A viral disease caused by a mosaic virus
options.D: A nematode disease of rice

questions.explanation: Bacterial blight of rice is caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae, often causing leaf blighting and drying.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is late blight of potato?

options.A: A destructive disease caused by Phytophthora infestans, a water mold (oomycete), which affects leaves, stems and tubers
options.B: A bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas
options.C: A viral disease caused by a mosaic virus
options.D: A nematode disease of potato

questions.explanation: Late blight of potato is a destructive disease caused by Phytophthora infestans, a water mold (oomycete), which affects leaves, stems and tubers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is rust disease?

options.A: A group of plant diseases caused by rust fungi, often producing orange, brown or reddish spore pustules on leaves and stems
options.B: A bacterial disease producing water-soaked lesions
options.C: A viral disease producing mosaic patterns
options.D: A nematode disease producing root galls

questions.explanation: Rust disease is a group of plant diseases caused by rust fungi, often producing orange, brown or reddish spore pustules on leaves and stems.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is a crop pest?

options.A: An organism that damages crops or reduces yield or quality; pests include insects, mites, nematodes, rodents, birds and some pathogens
options.B: An organism that helps crops grow
options.C: A type of fertiliser
options.D: A type of irrigation method

questions.explanation: A crop pest is an organism that damages crops or reduces yield or quality; pests include insects, mites, nematodes, rodents, birds and some pathogens.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What are insect pests?

options.A: Insects that feed on or damage crop plants, stored produce or plant products, such as bollworms, stem borers, aphids and whiteflies
options.B: Insects that help in pollination only
options.C: Insects that decompose organic matter only
options.D: Insects that produce honey only

questions.explanation: Insect pests feed on or damage crop plants, stored produce or plant products, such as bollworms, stem borers, aphids and whiteflies.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is a weed?

options.A: A plant growing where it is unwanted and competing with crops for light, water, nutrients and space
options.B: A plant grown for food
options.C: A plant grown for fibre
options.D: A plant grown for ornamental purposes

questions.explanation: A weed is a plant growing where it is unwanted and competing with crops for light, water, nutrients and space.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is biological pest control?

options.A: Use of natural enemies or biological agents such as predators, parasitoids, pathogens and antagonistic microbes to suppress pests
options.B: Use of chemical pesticides only
options.C: Use of mechanical tools to remove pests
options.D: Use of crop rotation only

questions.explanation: Biological pest control uses natural enemies or biological agents such as predators, parasitoids, pathogens and antagonistic microbes to suppress pests.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of biological pest control?

options.A: Ladybird beetles against aphids, Trichogramma parasitoid wasps against some moth eggs, and Bacillus thuringiensis against susceptible insect larvae
options.B: Applying chemical insecticides only
options.C: Using only mechanical traps
options.D: Burning crop residues

questions.explanation: Examples include ladybird beetles against aphids, Trichogramma parasitoid wasps against some moth eggs, and Bacillus thuringiensis against susceptible insect larvae.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is chemical pest control?

options.A: Use of pesticides or other chemical products to manage pests, diseases or weeds; selection and application must follow label directions and legal requirements
options.B: Use of natural enemies to suppress pests
options.C: Use of crop rotation to manage pests
options.D: Use of mechanical tools to remove pests

questions.explanation: Chemical pest control uses pesticides or other chemical products to manage pests, diseases or weeds; selection and application must follow label directions and legal requirements.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is integrated pest management (IPM)?

options.A: An ecosystem-based approach combining monitoring, prevention, cultural, mechanical, biological and carefully selected chemical methods to keep pests below economically damaging levels
options.B: An approach that uses only chemical pesticides
options.C: An approach that never uses any pesticides
options.D: An approach that uses only biological control

questions.explanation: IPM is an ecosystem-based approach combining monitoring, prevention, cultural, mechanical, biological and carefully selected chemical methods to keep pests below economically damaging levels.
questions.source: Agricultural Science Study Guide, Page 3 and Page 9

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What are cultural methods of pest control?

options.A: Crop rotation, resistant varieties, adjusted sowing dates, field sanitation, balanced fertilisation, intercropping and removal of infested residues
options.B: Use of chemical pesticides only
options.C: Use of biological predators only
options.D: Use of mechanical traps only

questions.explanation: Cultural methods include crop rotation, resistant varieties, adjusted sowing dates, field sanitation, balanced fertilisation, intercropping and removal of infested residues.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is an insecticide?

options.A: A pesticide intended to control insects
options.B: A pesticide intended to control weeds
options.C: A pesticide intended to control fungi
options.D: A pesticide intended to control nematodes

questions.explanation: An insecticide is a pesticide intended to control insects.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is a herbicide?

options.A: A pesticide intended to control insects
options.B: A pesticide intended to control unwanted plants or weeds
options.C: A pesticide intended to control fungi
options.D: A pesticide intended to control nematodes

questions.explanation: A herbicide is a pesticide intended to control unwanted plants or weeds.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is a fungicide?

options.A: A pesticide intended to control insects
options.B: A pesticide intended to control weeds
options.C: A pesticide intended to prevent or control fungal diseases; some products also act against oomycetes
options.D: A pesticide intended to control rodents

questions.explanation: A fungicide is a pesticide intended to prevent or control fungal diseases; some products also act against oomycetes.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is a pesticide?

options.A: A substance or mixture intended to prevent, destroy, repel or control pests, including insects, weeds, fungi and other organisms, as defined by applicable law
options.B: A substance used only to fertilise crops
options.C: A substance used only to irrigate crops
options.D: A substance used only to store crops

questions.explanation: A pesticide is a substance or mixture intended to prevent, destroy, repel or control pests, including insects, weeds, fungi and other organisms, as defined by applicable law.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is pesticide resistance?

options.A: The inherited ability of a pest population to survive a pesticide dose that previously controlled it, often selected by repeated use of the same mode of action
options.B: The inability of a pesticide to dissolve in water
options.C: The ability of a pesticide to kill all pests
options.D: The ability of a crop to grow without pesticides

questions.explanation: Pesticide resistance is the inherited ability of a pest population to survive a pesticide dose that previously controlled it, often selected by repeated use of the same mode of action.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: How can pesticide resistance be delayed?

options.A: Rotate modes of action, follow label rates, avoid unnecessary applications, use non-chemical methods and follow resistance-management guidance
options.B: Use the same pesticide repeatedly at any dose
options.C: Increase the dose beyond label recommendations
options.D: Apply pesticides more frequently than recommended

questions.explanation: Resistance can be delayed by rotating modes of action, following label rates, avoiding unnecessary applications, using non-chemical methods and following resistance-management guidance.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What are biopesticides?

options.A: Pest-control products based on microorganisms, natural substances or certain biological processes; examples include microbial agents and plant-derived compounds
options.B: Synthetic chemical pesticides only
options.C: Fertilisers containing only nitrogen
options.D: Irrigation water containing dissolved salts

questions.explanation: Biopesticides are pest-control products based on microorganisms, natural substances or certain biological processes; examples include microbial agents and plant-derived compounds.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What are biofertilisers?

options.A: Products containing living microorganisms that improve nutrient availability to plants through processes such as nitrogen fixation, phosphorus solubilisation or mycorrhizal association
options.B: Chemical fertilisers containing only NPK
options.C: Pesticides used to control insects
options.D: Organic manures produced by earthworms

questions.explanation: Biofertilisers are products containing living microorganisms that improve nutrient availability to plants through processes such as nitrogen fixation, phosphorus solubilisation or mycorrhizal association.
questions.source: Agricultural Science Study Guide, Page 3 and Page 9

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is Rhizobium?

options.A: A group of bacteria that form symbiotic nitrogen-fixing nodules on roots of many leguminous plants
options.B: A free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium found in soil
options.C: A symbiotic fungus associated with plant roots
options.D: A type of chemical fertiliser

questions.explanation: Rhizobium is a group of bacteria that form symbiotic nitrogen-fixing nodules on roots of many leguminous plants.
questions.source: Agricultural Science Study Guide, Page 3 and Page 9

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is Azotobacter?

options.A: A group of bacteria that form symbiotic nodules on legume roots
options.B: A free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium found in soil and used in some biofertiliser products
options.C: A symbiotic fungus associated with plant roots
options.D: A type of chemical fertiliser

questions.explanation: Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium found in soil and used in some biofertiliser products.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What are mycorrhizae?

options.A: Symbiotic associations between fungi and plant roots that can improve uptake of phosphorus, water and some micronutrients
options.B: Symbiotic associations between bacteria and legume roots
options.C: Free-living nitrogen-fixing bacteria
options.D: Chemical fertilisers containing phosphorus

questions.explanation: Mycorrhizae are symbiotic associations between fungi and plant roots that can improve uptake of phosphorus, water and some micronutrients.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is disease prevention in crops?

options.A: Use of clean seed and planting material, resistant varieties, crop rotation, sanitation, suitable spacing, balanced nutrition, vector management and timely diagnosis
options.B: Use of chemical pesticides only
options.C: Use of biological control only
options.D: Use of irrigation only

questions.explanation: Disease prevention in crops includes use of clean seed and planting material, resistant varieties, crop rotation, sanitation, suitable spacing, balanced nutrition, vector management and timely diagnosis.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: What is quarantine in plant protection?

options.A: Regulatory measures that prevent the introduction or spread of harmful plant pests and pathogens through movement of plants, seeds and plant products
options.B: The isolation of infected animals
options.C: The storage of harvested produce
options.D: The application of pesticides to crops

questions.explanation: Quarantine in plant protection refers to regulatory measures that prevent the introduction or spread of harmful plant pests and pathogens through movement of plants, seeds and plant products.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Plant Protection
questions.question: Why is pesticide safety important?

options.A: Incorrect handling can harm applicators, consumers, livestock, pollinators, soil organisms and aquatic ecosystems; use only registered products and follow official label precautions
options.B: Pesticides are harmless to all organisms
options.C: Pesticides can be used without any precautions
options.D: Pesticides only affect target pests

questions.explanation: Incorrect handling can harm applicators, consumers, livestock, pollinators, soil organisms and aquatic ecosystems; use only registered products and follow official label precautions.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is animal husbandry?

options.A: The science and practice of breeding, feeding, housing, caring for and managing domestic animals for useful products and services
options.B: The cultivation of crops only
options.C: The harvesting of fish only
options.D: The rearing of silkworms only

questions.explanation: Animal husbandry is the science and practice of breeding, feeding, housing, caring for and managing domestic animals for useful products and services.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is dairy farming?

options.A: Rearing and management of dairy animals for milk production, including breeding, feeding, health care and milk handling
options.B: Rearing chickens for meat production
options.C: Rearing sheep for wool production
options.D: Rearing fish in ponds

questions.explanation: Dairy farming is the rearing and management of dairy animals for milk production, including breeding, feeding, health care and milk handling.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: Which are common dairy cattle breeds in India?

options.A: Only Gir and Sahiwal
options.B: Indigenous breeds including Gir, Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar, Kankrej and Ongole; crossbred and exotic dairy cattle are also used
options.C: Only exotic breeds like Holstein Friesian
options.D: Only Tharparkar and Kankrej

questions.explanation: Indigenous dairy breeds include Gir, Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar, Kankrej and Ongole; crossbred and exotic dairy cattle are also used.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: Which cattle breeds are associated with Karnataka or adjoining Deccan regions?

options.A: Gir, Sahiwal and Red Sindhi
options.B: Amrit Mahal, Hallikar, Khillari and Deoni
options.C: Holstein Friesian and Jersey
options.D: Tharparkar and Ongole only

questions.explanation: Amrit Mahal, Hallikar, Khillari and Deoni are among recognised cattle breeds associated with Karnataka or adjoining Deccan regions; breed distribution may cross state boundaries.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is poultry farming?

options.A: Rearing domestic birds such as chickens, ducks and turkeys for eggs, meat and other products
options.B: Rearing cattle for milk production
options.C: Rearing sheep for wool production
options.D: Rearing fish in ponds

questions.explanation: Poultry farming is rearing domestic birds such as chickens, ducks and turkeys for eggs, meat and other products.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is broiler poultry?

options.A: Chickens raised mainly for meat production
options.B: Chickens managed mainly for egg production
options.C: Ducks raised for meat production
options.D: Turkeys raised for egg production

questions.explanation: Broiler poultry refers to chickens raised mainly for meat production.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is layer poultry?

options.A: Chickens raised mainly for meat production
options.B: Chickens managed mainly for egg production
options.C: Ducks raised for meat production
options.D: Turkeys raised for egg production

questions.explanation: Layer poultry refers to chickens managed mainly for egg production.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is sheep rearing?

options.A: Keeping sheep for meat, wool, milk, skins or manure, depending on breed and production system
options.B: Keeping goats for milk and meat only
options.C: Keeping cattle for milk production only
options.D: Keeping chickens for egg production only

questions.explanation: Sheep rearing is keeping sheep for meat, wool, milk, skins or manure, depending on breed and production system.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is goat rearing?

options.A: Keeping goats for milk, meat, fibre, skins and manure; goats are adapted to a range of environments but still require suitable feed and health care
options.B: Keeping sheep for wool production only
options.C: Keeping cattle for milk production only
options.D: Keeping chickens for meat production only

questions.explanation: Goat rearing is keeping goats for milk, meat, fibre, skins and manure; goats are adapted to a range of environments but still require suitable feed and health care.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is cattle breeding?

options.A: Selection and mating of cattle to improve traits such as milk yield, growth, fertility, disease resistance and adaptation
options.B: Feeding cattle with balanced ration only
options.C: Housing cattle in sheds only
options.D: Vaccinating cattle against diseases only

questions.explanation: Cattle breeding is the selection and mating of cattle to improve traits such as milk yield, growth, fertility, disease resistance and adaptation.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is crossbreeding?

options.A: Mating animals from different breeds to combine desirable traits or exploit hybrid vigour; outcomes depend on breed choice and management
options.B: Mating animals of the same breed only
options.C: Rearing animals without any breeding plan
options.D: Feeding animals with crossbred fodder only

questions.explanation: Crossbreeding is mating animals from different breeds to combine desirable traits or exploit hybrid vigour; outcomes depend on breed choice and management.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is animal nutrition?

options.A: The study and provision of nutrients required for maintenance, growth, reproduction, production and health
options.B: The study of animal breeding only
options.C: The study of animal housing only
options.D: The study of animal diseases only

questions.explanation: Animal nutrition is the study and provision of nutrients required for maintenance, growth, reproduction, production and health.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What are the main classes of nutrients in animal feed?

options.A: Water, carbohydrates, proteins, fats, minerals and vitamins
options.B: Only carbohydrates and proteins
options.C: Only minerals and vitamins
options.D: Only water and fats

questions.explanation: The main classes of nutrients in animal feed are water, carbohydrates, proteins, fats, minerals and vitamins.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Animal Husbandry and Allied Activities
questions.question: What is a balanced ration?

options.A: A feed mixture supplying required nutrients in appropriate amounts and proportions for an animal's species, age, body condition and production stage
options.B: A feed mixture containing only carbohydrates
options.C: A feed mixture containing only proteins
options.D: A feed mixture containing only minerals and vitamins

options.A: It is a central sector scheme providing income support of ₹6,000 per year
options.B: It is a crop-insurance scheme launched in 2016 to provide insurance coverage and financial support to farmers affected by specified crop losses
options.C: It is a programme focused on expanding irrigation access
options.D: It is a programme providing soil nutrient status and recommendations

questions.explanation: PMFBY is a crop-insurance scheme launched in 2016 to provide insurance coverage and financial support to farmers affected by specified crop losses due to notified risks, subject to scheme guidelines.
